entrypoints.summary: A connected computer invokes android.intent.action.MAIN directly on com.passbolt.mobile.android.feature.main.mainscreen.MainActivity through ADB activity-manager start.

negative_controls: The report states passwords cannot be viewed in plaintext.
The reported exposure ends when the currently allocated JWT expires.
observability.positive_marker: The authenticated portion of the app is displayed and its screens can be navigated without passphrase or fingerprint.

preconditions: The victim has logged in to the Android app.
The attacker can access an unlocked phone and use a computer connected to it.
The app has been switched away from and then closed; the report's procedure optionally enables fingerprint authentication.
The allocated JWT has not expired.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: ADB root followed by `adb shell am start -a "android.intent.action.MAIN" -n "com.passbolt.mobile.android.qa/com.passbolt.mobile.android.feature.main.mainscreen.MainActivity"`.
trigger_steps.summary: Directly start the named MainActivity with android.intent.action.MAIN using the report's ADB activity-manager command.

impacts.concept: Bypass of post-background application authentication lock

mitigations.concept: Lock-state enforcement on every activity entrypoint

relation_candidates.rationale: The report documents that directly starting MainActivity through ADB displays the authenticated application portion without the passphrase or fingerprint.
relation_candidates.src: Direct ADB invocation of an Android authenticated activity

relation_candidates.dst: Bypass of post-background application authentication lock
relation_candidates.rationale: The observed ability to navigate authenticated screens without the configured unlock mechanism is the stated lock-bypass effect.

relation_candidates.dst: Lock-state enforcement on every activity entrypoint
relation_candidates.rationale: The report recommends remaining locked even when activities are invoked directly from the command line.

sources.concept: Direct ADB invocation of an Android authenticated activity

impact.affected_asset: Authenticated Passbolt mobile application UI and its accessible account information; plaintext password display is explicitly excluded by the report.
impact.attacker_capability: Navigate authenticated Android application screens without the user's passphrase or fingerprint from an unlocked device using a connected computer.
impact.security_effect: Authentication-lock bypass for already-authenticated application content

causal_trace.summary: A user has logged in, switches away from the open app, and closes Passbolt; the app's feature is intended to require passphrase or fingerprint before authenticated use resumes.
Direct invocation of MainActivity does not enforce the lock feature's required passphrase-or-fingerprint reauthentication before exposing the authenticated application portion.
ADB activity-manager dispatch starts MainActivity with the MAIN action, providing an alternate activity entry route after backgrounding and closure.

A person with an unlocked phone and connected computer can navigate all authenticated screens without the passphrase or fingerprint while the allocated JWT remains valid; the report states its creation lifetime is five minutes and that passwords are not shown plaintext.

failure.operation: Direct Android activity launch to MainActivity bypasses the post-background authentication lock gate.

primary_invariant.statement: Every route that exposes authenticated application screens after the app's lock event must require the configured passphrase or fingerprint unlock.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The report's direct ADB launch of MainActivity displays and permits navigation of authenticated content without either credential after the ordinary background/closure sequence.

quality.review_notes: The public audit report provides a concrete reproduction command, prerequisites, observed UI result, JWT time bound, and recommendation. No Android manifest, lifecycle source, fixed patch, release mapping, or post-fix regression execution is present. The report lists `adb root` but does not characterize device/debug eligibility; reproducibility therefore depends on the assessed environment.

remediation.invariant_restored: Keep the app locked regardless of activities invoked directly from the command line, so a direct activity launch cannot expose authenticated screens before reauthentication.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Victim has logged in; attacker has access to the unlocked Android device and a connected computer, then invokes the documented ADB command after the app is switched away from and closed.
data_structure_invariants: Allocated JWT remains valid for a reported five-minute lifetime from creation.
Authenticated screens must not be exposed after the lock event without passphrase or fingerprint.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The report states exploitation is limited until expiry of the current JWT, whose lifetime from creation is five minutes.
numeric_domains.name: allocated JWT lifetime

state_context.state_machine: Logged-in application transitions through a switch-away/closure condition in which the lock feature should require passphrase or fingerprint before authenticated use; a direct MainActivity launch reaches authenticated UI instead.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Android QA package com.passbolt.mobile.android.qa assessed in Cure53 report dated 2021-12-13; no product release or source commit mapping is supplied.

oracle.channel: Android UI after ADB activity invocation
oracle.expected_negative: A lock-state-preserving implementation remains locked and requires the configured passphrase or fingerprint after the same direct activity launch.
oracle.expected_positive: After login, backgrounding, closing the app, and directly starting MainActivity through the documented ADB command, the vulnerable behavior is authenticated UI display and navigation without passphrase or fingerprint.
